title: How ABS Brakes Work in 60 Seconds 🚗🛑 #shorts
description:
Without ABS, slamming the brakes can lock the wheels so the car skids and won't steer. ABS uses a speed sensor at each wheel and a computer that spots a wheel slowing too fast, then valves release and reapply the brake pressure up to about 15 times a second. That's the pulsing you feel in the pedal, and it keeps the tires gripping so you can still steer. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#abs #brakes #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Slam the brakes without ABS and the wheels can *lock up*, so the car *won't steer*.

steps.label: Sensors
steps.text: A *speed sensor* at each wheel reads a *toothed ring* as it spins.

steps.label: Computer
steps.text: A small *computer* watches every wheel for one that suddenly *slows too fast*.

steps.label: Valves
steps.text: Then *valves* briefly *release the brake pressure* on that wheel, so it keeps turning.

steps.label: Pulsing
steps.text: This can repeat up to *15 times a second*, which you feel as a *pulsing pedal*.

steps.label: Grip
steps.text: The tires keep *gripping* the road, so you can still *steer* around danger.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Sense, release, *grip*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
